Canon writes a Paren node's parens once, and Faithful forgives a source pair
nested directly inside that pair (issue 01a1664d-75d4, perigrin's rulings of
2026-10-22 and round 7). perl keeps such a paren as one boolean bit,
OPf_PARENS (`P` in Concise), on the op it wraps, so `((x))` and `(x)` are
one tree. Each row's comment quotes perl 5.44.0's -MO=Concise.

=== a lexical in parens
my $x; my $z = ($x);
--- facts
faithful
# padsv[$x:1,3] sP; without the paren, padsv[$x:1,3] s

=== a package variable in parens
our $x; my $z = ($x);
--- facts
faithful
# ex-rv2sv sKP/1

=== a lexical in doubled parens
my $x; my $z = (($x));
--- facts
faithful
# padsv[$x:1,3] sP, as with one pair

=== a lexical in tripled parens
my $x; my $z = ((($x)));
--- facts
faithful

=== a comparison in parens as a call argument
sub ok {} our $y; ok(($y eq "x"));
--- facts
faithful
# seq sKPM/2; without the inner pair, seq sKM/2

=== a comparison in doubled parens as a call argument
sub ok {} our $y; ok((($y eq "x")));
--- facts
faithful
# seq sKPM/2, as with one pair

=== a call's parens around a parenthesised constant
print ((1))+2;
--- facts
faithful
# const[IV 1] sP; `print (1)+2` is const[IV 1] s. The outer pair is
# print's, so canon writes both.

=== a call's parens around a grouped term
print ((1+2)*3);
--- facts
faithful

=== a niladic call in parens before an arrow
sub f { (shift)->can("x") } f("main");
--- facts
faithful

=== a comparison chain in parens
my $x = 2; my $r = (1 < $x < 3);
--- facts
faithful

=== a list repeated, in doubled parens
my @r = ((1, 2)) x 2;
--- facts
faithful
# repeat lK/DOLIST,2, as with one pair

=== a scalar repeated, in doubled parens
our $y; my @r = (($y)) x 3;
--- facts
faithful
# repeat lK/DOLIST,2, as `($y) x 3`; `$y x 3` is the string repeat

=== a parenthesised not
our $x; my $r = (not $x);
--- facts
faithful
# not sKP/1

=== an element and its trailing comma inside parens
sub f {} f((0,));
--- facts
faithful

=== a parenthesised element before a trailing comma
sub f {} f((0),);
--- facts
faithful

=== a declared list and a declared name with a comma
my ($p, $q) = (1, 2); my $s, $q;
--- facts
faithful

=== an arrow call's argument in doubled parens
my $f = sub {}; our $x; $f->(($x));
--- facts
faithful
known-defect 01a16602-5f1a-7d56-a91d-5fa2c478d608
# ex-rv2sv sKPM/1; `$f->($x)` is ex-rv2sv sKM/1. psc's tree puts one
# Paren on $x for both pairs, though the outer is the call's, so canon
# writes `$f->($x)`.

=== not's operand in doubled parens
our $a; my $r = not (($a == 1));
--- facts
faithful
known-defect 01a16602-5f1a-7d56-a91d-5fa2c478d608
# eq sKP/2; `not ($a == 1)` is eq sK/2. psc's tree puts one Paren on the
# comparison for both pairs, though the outer is not's, so canon writes
# `not ($a == 1)`.

=== a list slice of a list
my $x = (1,2,3)[1];
--- facts
faithful
# ex-list lK: the slice's pair sets no OPf_PARENS bit

=== a list slice of an array
my @a; my @x = (@a)[0];
--- facts
faithful

=== a list slice of a list in doubled parens
my $x = ((1,2,3))[1];
--- facts
faithful
known-defect 01a16602-5f1a-7d56-a91d-5fa2c478d608
# ex-list lKP; `(1,2,3)[1]` is ex-list lK. psc's tree puts one Paren on
# the list for both pairs, though the outer is the slice's.

=== a list slice of a list in tripled parens
my $x = (((1,2,3)))[1];
--- facts
faithful
known-defect 01a16602-5f1a-7d56-a91d-5fa2c478d608

=== a list slice of stat in doubled parens
my $x = ((stat "/"))[2];
--- facts
faithful
known-defect 01a16602-5f1a-7d56-a91d-5fa2c478d608
# stat lKP; `(stat "/")[2]` is stat lK

=== a list slice of an array in doubled parens
my @a; my @x = ((@a))[0,1];
--- facts
faithful
known-defect 01a16602-5f1a-7d56-a91d-5fa2c478d608
# padav lP; `(@a)[0,1]` is padav l

=== a list slice of caller in doubled parens
my $x = ((caller))[2];
--- facts
faithful
known-defect 01a16602-5f1a-7d56-a91d-5fa2c478d608

=== a list slice in doubled parens assigned to a list
my @a; my ($p,$q) = ((@a))[0,1];
--- facts
faithful
known-defect 01a16602-5f1a-7d56-a91d-5fa2c478d608

=== a parenthesised element before a trailing comma, in parens
my @r = ((1),);
--- facts
faithful
# the same ops as `my @r = (1,);`

=== an element and its trailing comma in parens, before a trailing comma
sub f {} f((0,),);
--- facts
faithful
# the same ops as `f((0,))`

=== doubled parens around a product of a grouped sum
my ($a,$b); my $x = ((($a+$b)*2));
--- facts
faithful
# the same ops as `(($a+$b)*2)`
